sections.title: Hybrid Architecture (Venv Orchestration)
sections.content:
The Container / Autostart module is not a full-stack hypervisor like Docker. It does not virtualize kernel or network layers. Instead, it serves as a native Windows Orchestrator.

It clusters lightweight Python virtual environments into managed container groups. The result is instant startup and minimal RAM footprint (zero Docker daemon overhead) while maintaining auto-start, crash recovery, and memory monitoring.

sections.title: Importing Groups & Real-time Persistence
sections.content:
This module tightly integrates with the Multi-run tab. Groups are imported into the container manager:

  1. Configure your project group in the Multi-run tab.
  2. Navigate to Container and click ➕ Add New Group.
  3. Select the group from the catalog to generate its dedicated control widget.
Zero-Save Real-time Persistence: All configurations persist instantly. Toggling checkboxes or adjusting timers writes to individual JSON descriptors in assets/autostart_multi/ (or %APPDATA%) in milliseconds.

sections.title: Dashboard Metrics (LED, RAM & Modes)
sections.content:
Each imported widget operates as an independent telemetry dashboard.

1. Live Telemetry

  • Status LED: Real-time operational health indicator:
    • Gray: Empty group without projects.
    • Red: All processes are currently stopped.
    • Green: Live runtime active with zero failure states.
    • Flashing Orange: Crash state detected in one or more child processes.
  • Recursive RAM Monitor: Polls memory every 2 seconds, recursively summing memory across all subprocesses and worker threads.

2. Header Controls

  • Autostart: Automatically boots the container group on application launch.
  • T (Terminal) vs S (Silent): Launch mode (T = active CMD console for debugging; S = headless background execution).
Silent Mode Management: Even in silent mode, Windows Job Objects automatically terminate child runtimes on app exit. Always use the STOP button for clean shutdown.

sections.title: Sequencing, Signal Anchors & Stability
sections.content:
Container launches are coordinated by a dedicated Launch Worker enforcing sequential execution and Chain Stability.

1. Intelligent Wait Timers

The Wait (s) parameter delays process startup. During countdown, VenvHub evaluates predecessor health every 500ms. If a predecessor crashes, the countdown pauses, resets, and waits for predecessor recovery.

2. Signal Anchors (Hook Handshake)

Anchors provide precise synchronization for asynchronous servers:

  • Unique Handshake Key: Injects the signal path into VENVHUB_KOTVA.
  • Queue Blocking: Halts startup until the Python runtime writes the anchor file to disk.

Python Anchor Implementation:

import os

def signal_ready():
    hook_path = os.environ.get("VENVHUB_KOTVA")
    if hook_path:
        try:
            with open(hook_path, 'w') as f:
                pass
            print("⚓ Anchor: Signal dispatched.")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️ Anchor error: {e}")

# Call once server initialization completes
signal_ready()

sections.title: Crash Detection & 3-Strike Respawn
sections.content:
1. Cascade Failure Prevention

  • Grace Period (6s): Temporarily ignores process states during initial console boot.
  • Fatal Break: If a predecessor fails 3 consecutive launch attempts, the sequence halts permanently (🛑 FATAL ERROR) to prevent dependency deadlock.

2. Runtime Respawn (3-Strike Rule)

If a service crashes during normal operation:

  • Audit: Records crash telemetry to crash_log.jsonl inside the Venv directory.
  • Hard Cleanup: Waits 2 seconds, kills orphaned windows, and releases network sockets.
  • Reincarnation: Relaunches the process with preserved working directory.
  • 3-Strike Rule: After 3 sequential crashes, respawns lock to preserve console diagnostics.
Resetting Counters: Clicking STOP on the container widget resets all failure counters and clears 3-Strike locks.

sections.title: System Boot Lifecycle & Ownership Matrix
sections.content:
Application Boot Engine

On startup, AutostartBooter evaluates groups marked for Autostart. If conflicting processes are already active on host ports, Autostart safely aborts to prevent collisions.

Process Ownership Matrix

Child processes bind strictly to their parent group context in memory. Issuing a Stop command to Group B never affects concurrent processes owned by Group A.
